title: Constant (d,k) algorithm: Voronoi-partition enumeration is not specified (Prop. prop:dk)

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
Proposition prop:dk correctly BOUNDS the number of $k$-center Voronoi partitions by $n^{O(dk)}$ using the sign-pattern (Warren / Sauer-Shelah) argument. However the actual ENUMERATION is hand-waved: 'enumerate one representative partition for each realizable sign pattern (e.g. by sweeping over the $n^{O(dk)}$ combinatorially distinct centroid configurations, each a choice of which data points are co-decisive for the $\binom{k}{2}$ bisectors)'.

Problems:
(1) A COUNT of sign patterns does not yield a GENERATOR of representatives in matching time.
(2) 'Choice of which data points are co-decisive for the bisectors' is undefined and does not obviously produce an $n^{O(dk)}$-time enumeration.
(3) There is no proof that the OPTIMAL Voronoi partition is among the enumerated representatives.

The result itself is true (Inaba-Katoh-Imai 1994). To close the gap, give an explicit algorithm (in an algorithm box with Input/Output) that enumerates candidate partitions via the arrangement of the $O(n^2)$ pairwise bisector hyperplanes (or candidate centroids as subset means), prove via the centroid lemma (lem:centroid) that the optimal partition is generated, and bound the running time by $n^{O(dk)}$ rigorously.
